## High-Skilled Mobility & Location Choice {#high-skilled-mobility}

::: {.output-list .editorial-list}
::: {#urban-network-biomedical-mobility .output-item .output-item-priority}
<h3>Spatial Structure and Determinants of Global Top Biomedical Scientists' Mobility from an Urban Network Perspective <span class="status-badge status-accepted">Accepted</span> <span class="status-badge status-output">First Author</span></h3>
<p><strong>Focus:</strong> intercity mobility networks of global top biomedical scientists, career-stage differences, and city-level factors associated with mobility ties.</p>
<p><strong>Data:</strong> 500 scientists; 1970-2023 career histories; 398 cities; 1,440 mobility links.</p>
<p><strong>Methods:</strong> career-history reconstruction; directed weighted mobility network; SNA; GIS; Heckman two-step.</p>
<p class="detail-link"><a class="publication-link" href="papers/urban-network-biomedical-mobility.html">Details →</a></p>
:::

::: {#whole-ego-mobility .output-item}
<h3>Structure and Formation Mechanisms of Intercity Mobility Networks of Global Top Biomedical Scientists: A Whole-Network and Ego-Network Perspective <span class="status-badge status-submitted">Submitted</span> <span class="status-badge status-output">First Author</span></h3>
<p><strong>Focus:</strong> whole-network structure, ego-network position, career trajectories, and city conditions in global biomedical scientist mobility.</p>
<p><strong>Data:</strong> long-term top-scientist career histories; city-level mobility ties; ego-network subsample; collaboration and career-stage information.</p>
<p><strong>Methods:</strong> whole-network analysis; ego-network analysis; constraint; effective size; Shannon entropy; weighted ERGM; GIS.</p>
<p class="detail-link"><a class="publication-link" href="papers/whole-ego-mobility.html">Details →</a></p>
:::

::: {#pre-move-coauthor-ties .output-item}
<h3>Pre-move coauthor ties and the direction of scientific mobility: A city-level choice analysis of highly cited biomedical scientists <span class="status-badge status-submitted">Submitted</span> <span class="status-badge status-output">First Author</span></h3>
<p><strong>Focus:</strong> whether pre-move direct coauthor ties distinguish selected destination cities from candidate alternatives.</p>
<p><strong>Data:</strong> observed mobility events; focal scientists; event-specific candidate-city choice sets; pre-move coauthor ties.</p>
<p><strong>Methods:</strong> candidate-set construction; conditional logit; pre-move tie measurement; distance and city-level controls; robustness and timing checks.</p>
<p class="detail-link"><a class="publication-link" href="papers/pre-move-coauthor-ties.html">Details →</a></p>
:::
:::

:::

## Scientific Collaboration Networks & Relational Dynamics {#scientific-collaboration}

::: {.output-list .editorial-list}
::: {#after-collaboration-goes-quiet .output-item}
<h3>When Coauthorship Goes Quiet: Relational History, Portfolio Context, and the Recurrence of Scientific Ties <span class="status-badge status-submitted">Submitted</span> <span class="status-badge status-output">First Author</span></h3>
<p><strong>Focus:</strong> associations among coauthorship recurrence after publication dormancy, prior relationship history, active collaboration portfolios, and elapsed dormancy.</p>
<p><strong>Data:</strong> longitudinal focal-scientist publication records; recurrent dormant coauthor spells; annual risk-year observations.</p>
<p><strong>Methods:</strong> discrete-time complementary-log-log event-history model; clustered covariance; standardized predictions; dormancy-threshold robustness.</p>
<p class="detail-link"><a class="publication-link" href="papers/after-collaboration-goes-quiet.html">Details →</a></p>
:::
:::

## Corporate Innovation & Knowledge Assets {#corporate-innovation}

::: {.output-list .editorial-list}
::: {#firm-year-innovation-data .output-item}
<h3>Firm-Year Innovation Data System <span class="status-badge status-output">Data System in Progress</span></h3>
<p><strong>Focus:</strong> connects R&D expenditure, patents, trademarks, industry, country, firm identity, and year for leading global R&D firms.</p>
<p><strong>Data:</strong> high-R&D firms; patents; trademarks; industry and country fields.</p>
<p><strong>Methods:</strong> entity matching; intellectual-property linkage; panel construction; measurement audit.</p>
<p class="detail-link"><a class="publication-link" href="papers/firm-year-innovation-data.html">Details →</a></p>
:::

::: {#technology-brand-portfolios .output-item}
<h3>Technology-Brand Innovation Portfolios <span class="status-badge status-output">Research Design and Data Construction in Progress</span></h3>
<p><strong>Focus:</strong> compares how patent portfolios and trademark portfolios co-appear without reducing innovation to a single output count.</p>
<p><strong>Data:</strong> linked intellectual-property records; firm-year observations.</p>
<p><strong>Methods:</strong> indicator construction; portfolio comparison; type description.</p>
<p class="detail-link"><a class="publication-link" href="papers/technology-brand-innovation-portfolios.html">Details →</a></p>
:::

::: {#dynamic-evolution-spatial-context .output-item}
<h3>Dynamic Evolution and Spatial Context</h3>
<p><strong>Focus:</strong> examines how innovation portfolios vary over time with industry, country, firm characteristics, and regional innovation environments.</p>
<p><strong>Data:</strong> annual firm innovation records; industry and country context.</p>
<p><strong>Methods:</strong> measurement framework under development; no additional model is publicly specified at this stage.</p>
<p class="detail-link"><a class="publication-link" href="papers/dynamic-evolution-spatial-context.html">Details →</a></p>
:::
:::

## Early Research {#early-research}

::: {.output-list .editorial-list}
::: {#china-us-biomedical-innovation .output-item}
<h3>A Comparative Study of Biomedical Innovation in China and the United States from a Talent-Mobility Network Perspective</h3>
<p><strong>Focus:</strong> compares biomedical innovation systems in China and the United States through the movement and network position of top scientists.</p>
<p><strong>Data:</strong> top biomedical scientists in China and the United States; career histories; publications; patent and innovation-system materials.</p>
<p><strong>Methods:</strong> CV analysis; social network analysis; comparative innovation-system analysis; talent-mobility network analysis.</p>
<p class="detail-link"><a class="publication-link" href="papers/china-us-biomedical-innovation.html">Details →</a></p>
:::

::: {#urban-resilience-nighttime-lights .output-item}
<h3>Urban Resilience Assessment Based on Nighttime-Light Remote Sensing and Fisher Information</h3>
<p><strong>Focus:</strong> evaluates short-term urban resilience changes during the COVID-19 shock through nighttime-light dynamics.</p>
<p><strong>Data:</strong> VIIRS-DNB nighttime-light observations; 2019-2020 comparison; major Chinese urban agglomerations; city-level time series.</p>
<p><strong>Methods:</strong> Fisher Information Light; adaptive-cycle framework; time-series comparison; Dynamic Time Warping; K-Means.</p>
<p class="detail-link"><a class="publication-link" href="papers/urban-resilience-nighttime-lights.html">Details →</a></p>
:::

::: {#global-trade-network .output-item}
<h3>Spatiotemporal Evolution of the Global Trade Network during the COVID-19 Pandemic</h3>
<p><strong>Focus:</strong> examines changes in the global commodity trade network and product-specific trade structures during the pandemic.</p>
<p><strong>Data:</strong> UN Comtrade; 2019-2021 commodity trade records; country and product-type trade networks.</p>
<p><strong>Methods:</strong> directed weighted trade networks; social network analysis; centrality, density, clustering, and path-length measures.</p>
<p class="detail-link"><a class="publication-link" href="papers/global-trade-network.html">Details →</a></p>
:::
:::

:::
